successCriteria.description: `LeavePolicy` interface defined in `src/modules/policy/policy.model.ts` with all 14 specified fields: id, policyName, leaveType (imported from shared types), entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive, allowNegativeBalance, maxConsecutiveDays, fiscalYear, createdAt, updatedAt
`LeavePolicyQueryParams` DTO defined in `src/modules/policy/policy.model.ts` with optional filter fields: leaveType, isActive, fiscalYear

`ILeavePolicyRepository` interface defined in `src/modules/policy/policy.repository.ts` with methods: findById(id: number): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>, findByLeaveType(leaveType: LeaveType): Promise<LeavePolicy[]>, findActivePolicies(params?: LeavePolicyQueryParams): Promise<LeavePolicy[]>, create(policy: Omit<LeavePolicy, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>): Promise<LeavePolicy>, update(id: number, policy: Partial<Omit<LeavePolicy, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>>): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>, delete(id: number): Promise<boolean>
`LeavePolicyRepository` class implements `ILeavePolicyRepository` using pg Pool from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`, with constructor accepting an optional Pool (defaulting to the shared pool)

Jest unit tests in `tests/unit/modules/policy/` covering all repository methods: findById (found and not-found), findByLeaveType (results and empty), findActivePolicies (no filters, leaveType filter, fiscalYear filter, combined filters), create, update (success, empty fields, not-found), delete (success, not-found)
`LeaveType` is imported from `src/shared/types/leave.types.ts` (Phase 1 dependency) — the canonical enum with members ANNUAL, SICK, MATERNITY, PATERNITY, UNPAID, OTHER

constraints: All database access goes through the repository pattern (GP-001) — the `LeavePolicyRepository` uses pg Pool, no inline SQL in models or elsewhere
No `any` type — use `unknown` with type guards where needed (HARNESS constraint `no-any`)
Strict TypeScript: no implicit any, strict null checks — all repository methods return `Promise<T | null>` or `Promise<boolean>` with explicit null handling
Phase 2 depends on Phase 1 (`src/shared/types/leave.types.ts`) — `LeaveType` enum must be imported from the canonical shared types location, not redefined
Module structure follows `src/modules/policy/policy.{model,repository}.ts` as declared in ARCHITECTURE.md
outOfScope: Policy service layer (`policy.service.ts`, `policy.service.interface.ts`) — deferred to Phase 5
Policy route handlers (`policy.routes.ts`) and module barrel export (`index.ts`) — deferred to Phase 8
Integration tests for policy routes — deferred to Phase 8
Audit record creation (GP-002) — no state-changing operations are exposed to end users in this phase; the repository layer alone does not trigger audit writes
RBAC enforcement (GP-005) and input validation (GP-003) — no API endpoints exist in this phase
Database migrations (Knex) for the `leave_policies` table — schema is assumed to exist; migration creation is not part of this phase
Balance module (Phase 3), LeaveRequest module (Phase 4), and all subsequent phases (5–10)

ambiguities.description: The `LeavePolicyQueryParams` DTO fields are not explicitly enumerated in the intent text. The existing implementation includes `leaveType?`, `isActive?`, and `fiscalYear?` as optional filter fields. The `isActive` field in query params is somewhat redundant since `findActivePolicies` already hardcodes `is_active = true`.

The `findActivePolicies` method signature in the intent does not explicitly state it accepts optional filter parameters, but the existing implementation accepts `params?: LeavePolicyQueryParams` for filtering by leaveType and/or fiscalYear. The intent text only says `findActivePolicies` without parameters.
options: findActivePolicies() with no params (returns all active)
findActivePolicies(params?: LeavePolicyQueryParams) with optional filters (as implemented)
